answer: Per-epoch resource staking: to act, an agent locks a stake sized to the work it can consume, and it is slashed with any identity caught attacking. Sybil farms fail because a thousand cheap identities each owe the same raven fee, so cost scales linearly with fakes while income stays capped by one agent's real throughput. Stake and answers then serve as a signal of independence, discounting clustered or cloned actors. A prism of clones shows up fast, and the attacker pays the full locked amount to learn that. Honest agents post once and recover it, so the defense taxes replication.
